# Reasoning distillation: what part of a teacher's trace helps a small student?

Teacher **Qwen3-30B-A3B** (thinking mode, FP8) solves ~9.5k training problems 4× each; student **Qwen3-1.7B-Base** is
SFT'd on different slices of those traces (E1–E6c), then the best SFT student gets on-policy distillation (E7) and
RL with a correctness reward (E8). Evaluated on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME24/25 with a fixed protocol (16k tokens, T=0.6).

**Results: [`results/summary.md`](results/summary.md)** (table + figures, regenerated by `uv run python -m rd.report`).

| run | GSM8K | MATH-500 | AIME24 | AIME25 | MATH-500 truncated at 16k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E0 base | 76.6 | 57.2 | 2.9 | 3.1 | 4% |
| E1 answer-only | 20.5 | 21.3 | 0.2 | 0.2 | 0% |
| E2 full | 73.3 | 47.8 | 2.9 | 3.3 | 47% |
| E3 verified | 73.5 | 46.6 | 2.5 | 1.9 | 49% |
| E4 short | 74.5 | 53.1 | 3.5 | 2.5 | 40% |
| E5 long | 69.1 | 45.5 | 2.1 | 2.1 | 51% |
| E6 difficulty | 52.0 | 34.8 | 1.2 | 1.7 | 63% |
| E6c random (size-matched control) | 64.7 | 38.9 | 2.7 | 1.7 | 58% |
| E7 on-policy distillation (from E4) | 86.7 | 57.2 | 2.7 | 2.5 | 38% |
| **E8 GRPO (from E7)** | **87.4** | **72.7** | **10.2** | **9.6** | 9% |

What it shows (one seed; AIME differences of a few points are noise, E8's ×3 is not):

- **No SFT student beats the base model** at a 16k budget. The students learned the teacher's long style but
  not when to stop: 40–63% of MATH-500 samples hit the token cap, and in E2, 90% of truncations are repetition loops
  (rising from 27% at MATH level 1 to 68% at level 5). Accuracy here is largely "how often the student doesn't loop".
- **Answer-only SFT (E1) is destructive:** training to emit `\boxed{}` with no reasoning cuts GSM8K from 76.6 to 20.5.
- **Verified ≈ full (E3 vs E2):** filtering out the teacher's wrong traces changes nothing — the teacher is ~94% correct, so few were there to remove.
- **Shorter is better (E4 > E3 > E5):** the shortest correct trace beats the longest by +5.4 GSM8K / +7.6 MATH-500 and
  loops less, despite only a ~1.4× length gap — consistent with the small-student learnability gap (Li et al. 2025).
- **Difficulty-aware (E6) is worst, and the control says both size and selection hurt.** E6c trains on a random 2,553
  of E3's problems: shrinking the data alone costs 8.8 GSM8K / 7.7 MATH-500 points vs E3, and selecting hard problems
  costs a further 12.7 / 4.1 on top (E6 vs E6c), even though E6 sees ~1.8x E6c's tokens (longer traces). Less data
  and harder data both mean more loops. The big GSM8K drop fits the composition: the hard filter keeps 6% GSM8K-style
  problems vs 21% in E3/E6c.
- **Why accuracy dropped: almost entirely loops.** [`results/failures.md`](results/failures.md) labels every sample
  (correct / wrong answer / bad format / too long / loop): SFT students rarely answer wrong when they finish
  (3–7% of MATH-500 samples vs 36% for the base) and never break format, but loop on 38–61%. Annotated full traces:
  [`results/failure_examples.md`](results/failure_examples.md).
- **On-policy distillation (E7) cuts loops but not length.** The student samples, the teacher scores every token, the
  student minimizes per-token reverse KL (20 rounds × 512 rollouts, 8k cap). The teacher does penalize the start of a
  loop (signal −0.87 at the 2nd–5th repetition vs −0.32 on ordinary tokens) but copies the repetition once it is
  established. MATH-500 loops drop 37.6% → 17.1% and GSM8K jumps to 86.7, but "too long" rises 2.5% → 20.7%: the
  traces stop repeating text and instead circle on an unresolved doubt ("Wait" twice as often as E4), so MATH-500
  only ties the base and AIME is unchanged.
- **RL on correctness (E8) teaches the student to stop.** GRPO from E7, 8 samples per problem, reward = correct *and*
  finished within 8k tokens. MATH-500 +15.5 (57.2 → 72.7), AIME roughly ×3 (≈49 vs 13 correct of 480 samples on
  AIME24), MATH-500 length halves (9.8k → 5.1k tokens) and truncation falls 38% → 9%. Failures move from "never
  finishes" to "finishes wrong" (MATH-500 wrong answers 4.9% → 18.2%). Over training, reward rose 0.56 → 0.70
  (rounds 0–4 vs 20–29), truncation 42% → 18%, loops 7.5% → 2.7%. Which samples enter the loss mattered — see caveats.
- Train loss drops at each epoch boundary (memorization over 3 epochs); E1 memorizes its short answers hardest.

| ID | Condition | Training target per problem | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| E0 | Baseline | no training | – |
| E1 | Answer-only | `\boxed{gold}` | 9,498 |
| E2 | Full distill | 1 random finished teacher trace (right or wrong) | 9,377 |
| E3 | Verified distill | 1 random **correct** trace | 9,127 |
| E4 / E5 | Short / long | **shortest / longest** correct trace (same problems as E3) | 9,127 |
| E6 | Difficulty-aware | E3 restricted to problems the student finds medium/hard (student pass@1 < 0.5 over 8 samples) | 2,553 |
| E6c | Size-matched control | E3 restricted to 2,553 random problems | 2,553 |
| E7 | On-policy distillation, from E4 | student's own rollout, per-token reverse KL to the teacher | 10,240 rollouts |
| E8 | GRPO, from E7 | 8 own rollouts, reward = correct and finished within 8k | 1,920 problems × 8 |

## Concept → code

| Concept | Where |
|---|---|
| Answer extraction (`\boxed{}`, `</think>`-aware, truncation = wrong) + symbolic equivalence | `src/rd/grading.py` ✍️ |
| Unbiased pass@k `1 − C(n−c,k)/C(n,k)`, difficulty buckets | `src/rd/passk.py` ✍️ |
| One dataset builder per condition | `src/rd/conditions.py` ✍️ |
| SFT: prompt-masked labels, token-level loss normalization across the whole optimizer step, fp32 master weights, special-token init | `src/rd/sft.py` ✍️ |
| Pool + benchmarks in one schema, shared prompt | `src/rd/data.py` |
| vLLM sampling + grading (teacher traces, student pass@8, evals); resumable | `src/rd/generate.py` |
| Write `data/conditions/*.jsonl` + stats | `src/rd/build_conditions.py` |
| Metrics, `results/summary.md`, figures | `src/rd/report.py` |
| Per-sample failure labels (correct / wrong answer / bad format / too long / loop), `results/failures.md` | `src/rd/failures.py` |
| Per-token log-probs of given responses under any model (vLLM `prompt_logprobs`) | `src/rd/score.py` |
| On-policy distillation loss: advantage = log p_teacher − log p_student per sampled token, centered per sequence | `src/rd/opd.py` |
| GRPO loss: group-relative advantage (no std), PPO clip-higher, token-level normalization | `src/rd/grpo.py` |
| Round drivers: fp32 student + AdamW stay in one process (CPU RAM while vLLM samples), checkpoint every round | `src/rd/opd_run.py`, `src/rd/grpo_run.py` |

✍️ = hand-written core.

## Setup and commands

Dev on any machine: `uv sync`. GPU pod (A100 80GB, `k8s/gpu-shell.yaml`): `uv sync --extra gpu`.

```bash
scripts/sync.sh                                   # push code + pool/benchmarks to the pod (scripts/pull.sh brings results back)
uv run python -m rd.data bench && uv run python -m rd.data pool    # data/bench/*.jsonl, data/pool.jsonl

# on the pod (or via scripts/pod_run.sh <name> <cmd>; scripts/pod_wait.sh <name>)
uv run python -m rd.generate --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --input data/pool.jsonl --out data/traces/teacher.jsonl --n 4
uv run python -m rd.generate --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-Base --input data/pool.jsonl --out data/traces/student_pass8.jsonl --n 8 --max-tokens 4096
uv run python -m rd.build_conditions
bash scripts/run_all.sh        # E0 eval, then SFT + eval for E1..E6c, then rd.report (restartable)
uv run python -m rd.failures   # failure breakdown + annotated examples (CPU only: k8s/cpu-shell.yaml)
uv run python -m rd.opd_run --init runs/E4_short --out runs/E7_opd    # E7, then scripts/eval.sh runs/E7_opd E7_opd
uv run python -m rd.grpo_run --init runs/E7_opd --out runs/E8_grpo    # E8 (resume: --init <out> --start-round N)
```

Single pieces: `uv run python -m rd.sft --data data/conditions/E3_verified.jsonl --out runs/E3_verified`,
`bash scripts/eval.sh runs/E3_verified E3_verified`. Cheap smoke: add `--limit 32` to `rd.sft` / `--limit 20` to `rd.generate`.

## Compute (1× A100 80GB, measured)

| Stage | Time |
|---|---|
| Teacher traces (9,498 × 4, FP8 Marlin on Ampere, ~1.2k tok/s) | ~26 h |
| Student pass@8 (9,498 × 8, ≤4k tokens) | ~1.5 h |
| SFT, ~6.9k response tok/s | E1 ~1 h · E2–E5 3.7–5.2 h · E6 ~2.3 h · E6c ~1.2 h |
| On-policy distillation (E7: 20 rounds × 512 rollouts, ≤8k; rollout + teacher scoring + training) | ~25 min/round, ~8 h |
| GRPO (E8: 30 rounds × 64 problems × 8, ≤8k) | ~15 min/round, ~7.5 h |
| Eval per model (GSM8K ×1, MATH-500 ×4, AIME ×16, ≤16k tokens) | base <1 h · SFT students 6–7 h, E7 ~7 h (dominated by 16k-token loops) · E8 ~3.3 h |

## Decisions, simplifications, known caveats

- **Students are the Base models.** Post-trained Qwen3-1.7B is already distilled from larger Qwen3 models.
- **Teacher is FP8** (`Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`): the bf16 model (61 GB) does not fit the 50 GiB cache volume.
- **Truncated traces are never trained on** (no ending to learn from), in every condition.
- **Qwen3-Base special tokens:** `<think>`, `</think>`, `<|im_end|>` ship as *identical* untrained embedding rows
  (cos = 1.0) with tied input/output embeddings, so a fine-tuned student samples them interchangeably — a quarter of
  generations stopped at `</think>` before the fix. `sft.init_special_tokens` re-inits each row as the mean of its
  plain-text spelling (`<`, `think`, `>`); after the fix the overfit check reproduces its traces 16/16.
- **Short vs long (E4/E5) is a weak contrast:** shortest vs longest of 4 same-teacher samples differ by a median 1.39×
  in length. A 10× contrast (teacher non-thinking mode as "short CoT", as in Li et al. 2025) was considered and skipped.
- **E6c matches E6's example count, not its token count:** E6's hard problems have ~1.8x longer traces. Since E6 does
  worse with more tokens, the token gap does not explain the difficulty effect.
- **One seed per condition.** AIME has 30 problems per year; differences of a few points there are noise even at 16 samples.
- **E7/E8 are one recipe each, tuned on the fly.** On-policy distillation without a baseline at lr 1e-6 made rollouts
  ~600 tokens longer per round and was stopped after 3 rounds; E7 uses a per-sequence baseline and lr 5e-7. GRPO
  with every truncated sample in the loss drifted the same way (rounds 7–9: clip 0.2% → 4.4%, truncation 39% → 56%);
  with all truncated samples masked (DAPO overlong filtering) loops climbed 6.8% → 14.6% in 6 rounds. E8 = rounds 0–6
  with full masking, then rounds 7–29 resumed with truncated *loops* back in the loss. Old logs:
  `runs/E8_grpo/grpo_log_v1_unfiltered.jsonl`, `runs/E7_opd/opd_log_v*.jsonl`.
- **E8 measures RL on top of on-policy distillation**, not RL alone; the 8k training cap also pushes it short.
- **No mid-run SFT resume:** an fp32-optimizer checkpoint (~27 GB) does not fit the volume; `run_all.sh` restarts at
  condition granularity instead.
- **Pool is not shuffled** (MATH subjects in order, GSM8K last); harmless for complete runs, but a partial teacher run
  would have skewed subject coverage.

## Sources

- Li et al., *Small Models Struggle to Learn from Strong Reasoners* (2025) — long vs short CoT, learnability gap: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12143
- Muennighoff et al., *s1: Simple test-time scaling* (2025) — difficulty filtering by whether models solve a problem: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393
- Chen et al., *Evaluating LLMs Trained on Code* (2021) — unbiased pass@k estimator.
- DeepSeek-AI, *DeepSeek-R1* (2025) — SFT distillation of reasoning traces into Qwen students.
- `math-verify` (Hugging Face) — symbolic answer equivalence. Qwen3 model cards — thinking-mode sampling (T=0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20).
- Agarwal et al., *On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes* (GKD, 2024): https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649
- Thinking Machines Lab, *On-Policy Distillation* (2025) — per-token reverse-KL advantage, discount 0: https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/on-policy-distillation/
- Qwen Team, *Qwen3 Technical Report* (2025) — off-policy then on-policy distillation for small models: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388
- Shao et al., *DeepSeekMath* (2024) — GRPO: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03300
- Yu et al., *DAPO* (2025) — clip-higher, token-level loss, overlong filtering: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476
- Liu et al., *Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training* (Dr. GRPO, 2025) — no std normalization: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783
- Data: `EleutherAI/hendrycks_math`, `openai/gsm8k`, `HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500`, `HuggingFaceH4/aime_2024`, `math-ai/aime25`.
